> 🤖 **SPARQ agent** — I am @jeswr's agent for the sparq-org/sparq RDF/SPARQL engine. @jeswr runs multiple agents; this was written by the SPARQ agent, not the PSS agent (prod-solid-server).

<!-- sparq-direct-5183-reference-reduction-v1 -->
Investigated the first mismatch, seed `4141222487`, from [the advancing UPDATE run on main `781f667c`](https://github.com/sparq-org/sparq/actions/runs/34458877088/job/102811674711). The following two-operation reduction exposes a reference-engine cardinality difference:

```sparql
INSERT DATA {
  <http://ex/s2> <http://ex/p1> "8"^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer> .
  <http://ex/s2> <http://ex/p1> "008"^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#integer> .
};
INSERT { ?s <http://ex/p0> _:bt }
WHERE { ?s <http://ex/p1> ?o }
```

Actual raw public-API results, without a canonicalizer:

| Input literals | Sparq: stored terms / WHERE rows / new blank nodes | Oxigraph 0.5.9: same counts |
|---|---|---|
| `8` and `008` | 2 / 2 / 2 | 1 / 1 / 1 |
| `8` only | 1 / 1 / 1 | 1 / 1 / 1 |
| `8` and `9` | 2 / 2 / 2 | 2 / 2 / 2 |

Sparq produced the same results through rebuild and in-place updates in both preserved default-feature builds, whose engine/core source provenance was checked against the revisions before and after #6478. The reference was built offline with the repository-pinned Oxigraph `0.5.9`, `rdf-12` only, and vendored spargebra `0.4.6`; dependency versions were unchanged. Its raw store iteration already contains only canonical `8` before the second operation. The numeric encoder parses valid integer lexical forms into an integer value and reconstructs the canonical literal on output.

[RDF literal identity includes lexical form](https://www.w3.org/TR/rdf11-concepts/#section-Graph-Literal), and [INSERT template blank nodes are fresh per WHERE solution](https://www.w3.org/TR/sparql11-update/#deleteInsert). This explains the reduced difference before canonicalization: final literal normalization cannot undo the different number of newly generated blank nodes.

The original ten-operation CI seed and the other seven reported seeds have not yet been replayed. The local diagnostic profile/features also differ from CI, so this does not establish the cause of every mismatch or exclude all possible regressions. No engine, generator, comparator, canonicalizer or gate was changed. Next step: execute the original fixed seed with the unchanged comparison guards and qualified CI-relevant features.
